summary: The bill amends the Defense Production Act to add the Secretary of Agriculture to CFIUS, expand its jurisdiction to cover foreign investments in US agricultural businesses and farmland, and require the President to block any such transactions involving persons from China, Russia, Iran, or North Korea, while directing USDA to issue regular risk reports.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends CFIUS procedures under the Defense Production Act to add the Secretary of Agriculture and expand review of agricultural transactions by foreign persons from certain countries. It contains no provisions altering federal spending levels, appropriations, or budgets.
The bill focuses exclusively on foreign investment screening in agriculture and makes no changes to tax law, rates, credits, or revenue measures.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
The legislation has no connection to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
No immigration pathways, border enforcement, or visa provisions are present.
The bill does not address reproductive rights or abortion access.
While the bill amends the Defense Production Act and involves CFIUS (a national-security body), it does not alter military or defense spending levels.
No environmental regulations, protections, or climate-related measures are included.
The bill contains no welfare, nutrition assistance, or social safety-net provisions.
No education funding, school choice, or federal education policy changes appear in the text.
The legislation does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
No sentencing, policing, or criminal-justice reforms are present.

The bill expands CFIUS review to agricultural businesses and real estate and mandates prohibition of certain investments by persons from China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. This adds national-security-based restrictions on foreign investment, constituting a protectionist measure that limits open investment flows from designated adversaries.
No deficit, debt ceiling, or fiscal-balance provisions are included.
The bill does not address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil-rights issues.
No foreign-assistance funding or policy changes are present.
The legislation contains no voting-access, election-integrity, or campaign-related provisions.
Although biotechnology related to agriculture is mentioned in the CFIUS expansion, the bill addresses investment screening rather than data privacy or technology regulation.
No labor, union, or worker-protection measures are included.
The bill does not address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
